name: Multi-Sector F+ Kinetic-Scalar Decoupling
claimed_mechanism: This architecture decouples the MOND dynamics (handled by an auxiliary chi governed by a spatially nonlocal F+ operator) from the propagating scalar phi_k (which carries the lensing degrees of freedom). The MOND sector is algebraic in chi, avoiding the lapse-weighting trap (P3) and ensuring the preferred-frame response is screened by e^-y through the F+ kernel. The phi_k field has a standard, independent kinetic term, ensuring a finite normalization that is not screened out, thus avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wound. This separation allows the MOND strength, lensing carrier, and kinetic normalization to be distinct, satisfying the core cooking rule.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the MOND dynamics are reproduced by the nonlocal F+ kernel, which yields the correct mu(y) behavior. The lensing is carried by phi_k, which provides the necessary linear stress to source Psi without being constrained by the MOND sector's screening. The kinetic normalization of phi_k remains finite, ensuring no strong coupling. The preferred-frame response is screened by e^-y, keeping PPN parameters within bounds.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 because it includes a spatially nonlocal F+ kernel, which is not allowed in the local no-preferred-frame class. It is inequivalent to DC-002 because it does not use a standard timelike vector field for the aether. It is inequivalent to DC-003 because it does not use lapse-weighted MOND. It is inequivalent to DC-010 because it does not rely on a khronon field with a finite alpha_inf, which was killed by GW170817. The multi-sector structure with an independent kinetic scalar is a new architectural feature not present in any dead class.
